thread:
marco: quick follow-up from this morning's RFC — proposal to do an incremental RBAC shim rollout for dashboard tiles + query routing. want to lock on canary plan and perf validation before i wire the automation.

sarah: +1, thanks for running the doc. two quick constraints: (1) the shim must support both pushdown and fallback to the proxy for legacy tenants, (2) we need <100ms p95 added latency on the fast path.

marco: noted. the idea is: start with read-only routes, tile rendering only. rollout phases: canary 1% -> 10% -> 50% -> 100% with manual pause points. each step runs a perf harness and a correctness pass vs golden prompts.

dan: how will we gate the 10% -> 50% jump? curious about traffic skew for tenants that have heavy dashboard loads.

marco: plan is traffic-aware ramp: we pick tenants by percentile of QPS+avg tile size, pick low-impact tenants first. ramp only if latency + error delta < threshold for 15m. otherwise revert. automation will check metrics and roll back.

priya: for the authz cache: do we do a local in-process TTL cache or centralized sidecar? tradeoffs: local = super-fast but invalidation harder; sidecar = easier invalidation but adds RPC hop.

marco: good callout. i'm leaning local LRU with short TTL + an invalidation stream for role updates. rationale: most reads are repeated within short time windows, and sidecar hop kills our latency budget.

sarah: agree local LRU w/invalidation makes sense. ensure we emit cache-hit/miss telemetry and have an env flag to switch to sidecar for load tests.

dan: can we add a health-check route that returns "authz-state" so ops can detect mismatch between sidecars and shims? would help during cutover.

marco: yes — will add a /_debug/authz-status that reports last invalidation seq and cache age. only exposed to internal nets.

ops-bot: deploy scheduled: eng-platform/cutover/rbac-shim-canary @ 2024-11-03T18:00Z by marco. will post status updates.

priya: concerning correctness — how do we run acceptance? rendering correctness is tricky because of small differences in query planner ordering.

marco: acceptance will be sampled diff checks on the rendered JSON model. golden set + fuzzy compare tolerating ordering differences. also unit tests for decision trees (allow/deny paths) and an e2e with a few tenant fixtures.

sarah: perf harness requirements? i can pair with infra to generate synthetic tile requests across sequence lengths and KV cache sizes.

marco: perf plan in brief:
```
- baseline: current prod (no shim)
- canary-run: shim enabled for canary tenants
- metrics: p50/p95 latency, CPU/GPU util if applicable, authz cache hit rate, added RPCs
- acceptance: p95_added <= 20ms AND error_rate_delta <= 0.01
```

dan: curious about fallback semantics — if shim returns error, do we fallback to proxy synchronously or queue async?

marco: sync fallback to proxy (same request) for now. async queueing is a longer-term perf optimization but adds complexity for freshness.

priya: what about roll-forward compatibility? we need a header/flag that indicates shim-capable so older proxies don't break.

marco: will add X-Redwood-Shim: enabled|disabled header. proxies ignore unknown headers. also will support a feature-flag store so we can flip tenant-level behavior.

sarah: logging: ensure we tag logs with tenant_id, tile_type, shim_state (hit/miss/fallback) and sample traces for 1/1000 requests.

marco: agreed. telemetry will include these metrics + canary-specific dashboards (canary vs baseline overlays).

dan: any DB migrations or schema changes? authz needs a small role-lookup index but no user-facing schemas.

marco: just index addition (non-blocking). infra will apply in maintenance window prior to canary.

priya: timeline? i'd like at least 48h soak after 10% before 50%.

marco: proposed timeline:
- today: finalize config & automation
- +3d: perf tests + infra index
- +5d: canary 1% (smoke)
- +7d: 10% soak (48h)
- +10d: 50% (48h)
- +13d: 100%

sarah: looks reasonable. please add rollback playbook to the doc (metrics thresholds + manual steps).

marco: will add rollback steps and a checklist for ops. pinging @priya and @dan for final review before i open the PR. :eyes:

priya: will review today. :+1:

dan: ok from me, small nit: add an example invalidation event payload in the doc.

marco: done, pushed to the RFC doc. thanks everyone. will kick off automation once PR lands.
